[{"page_content": "5. Delivery SLAs
Delivery Service Level Agreements (SLAs) define expected delivery ranges after an order is confirmed and
released for fulfillment. An SLA is an operational target and does not mean that every parcel is guaranteed to
arrive at the exact end of the stated range.
5.1 Domestic Delivery SLA
Service Processing target Delivery target Typical total
Standard 0–2 business days 2–5 business days 2–7 business days
Express 0–1 business day 1–2 business days 1–3 business days
Priority metro Same/next business day 1 business day 1–2 business days
Large-item delivery 1–3 business days 3–7 business days 4–10 business days
Business days exclude weekends and configured public holidays. Weather events, carrier disruptions, customs
processing, remote-area restrictions, and customer-requested delivery changes can extend the operational timeline.
5.2 Delivery Status Definitions
Order confirmedmeans payment and order validation have succeeded.
Processing means the order is being prepared but has not necessarily been handed to the carrier.
Shipped/in transitmeans the parcel has entered the carrier network.
Out for deliverymeans the carrier has assigned the parcel to a delivery route.
Delivered means the carrier reports a successful delivery event.
Delivery exceptionmeans a carrier or operational issue is preventing normal progress.
5.3 Late Delivery
A customer should normally be treated as experiencing a late delivery when the current date exceeds the
applicable promised delivery range without an approved exception.
For standard domestic parcels, support should first inspect tracking data. If there has been no carrier scan for
48 hours while the parcel is in transit, the support agent may open a carrier investigation.
A delayed parcel should not automatically be declared lost. The lost-package workflow requires the applicable
investigation threshold to be reached.

Missing, Delayed, or Lost Package Policy
A package is considered potentially lost when carrier tracking has remained inactive beyond the investigation
threshold or the carrier explicitly confirms loss.
For domestic shipments, support may initiate a carrier investigation after 48 hours without movement when the
parcel is already outside its expected delivery range. For high-value shipments, the threshold may be reduced
when the tracking event indicates a serious exception.
A customer should not be asked to reorder immediately unless there is a clear business reason. Depending on
inventory and customer preference, Nimbus Commerce may provide a replacement or refund after the appropriate
investigation stage.
If the carrier confirms delivery but the customer cannot locate the parcel, support should verify delivery
coordinates or proof-of-delivery information where available. The customer may be asked to check common
delivery locations and household or building recipients before a claim is opened.

Order-Cancellation Policy
Customers can request cancellation before an order reaches a non-cancellable fulfillment stage.
8.1 Cancellation by Status
Order status Cancellation
Payment pending Normally allowed
Confirmed Usually allowed if fulfillment has not started
Processing Case-dependent
Packed Usually not cancellable
Shipped Not cancellable; customer may use return process
Out for delivery Not cancellable
Delivered Return process applies
Cancellation is a request, not a guarantee. If the warehouse has already packed or transferred the parcel to a
carrier, cancellation may no longer be operationally possible.
8.2 Cancellation Refund
If cancellation is approved before shipment, Nimbus Commerce initiates the refund according to the payment
method. Online payment refunds generally follow the payment provider’s processing time.
COD orders that are cancelled before dispatch do not require a COD refund because no cash payment was
collected.
8.3 Customer Refuses Delivery
Refusing delivery is not the preferred cancellation method. The customer should request cancellation before
shipment where possible. A refused parcel may incur operational handling costs and can delay the refund.
